The 'decisive proof' there compared 154 __data SECTIONS (packed into one segment) with 109 sections; sections are not the budgeted unit, segments are.
laws.counterexamples_checked: Tried to move the cap with: state shape (6 shapes + mixed), dim0=1 / dim1=1 / dim1=16 record variants, plain io 1..100, op chains and kinds, fp32/int32 plain io dtypes (add no segment), read-only state, partial exposure, h16g. Only removing the shared output segment altogether (no outputs) moved it (+1). Not testable: write-only state (frontend InvalidMILProgram), slice_update without write_state (MIL validation rejects), constant update source (InvalidMILProgram), no plain input (InvalidMILProgram), dead inputs / dead op chains (CompilationFailure).

laws.statement: Mechanism behind the cap (inferred from the compiled HWX, not from allocator source): every __FVMLIB segment of the output Mach-O is one BAR ordinal (0..54) and the compiler keeps the Mach-O at <= 57 LC_SEGMENT_64 (= <= 55 __FVMLIB/__KERN_* segments + __PAGEZERO + __TEXT). The unpacked layout is one segment per __data section [N state surfaces + K copy-out buffers of exposed states + OUT plain outputs] and one per __const section [IN plain inputs], plus one __KERN_0 lookup-table segment if the program has a LUT op (sigmoid/tanh/softmax/gelu/silu/erf/exp/log/inverse/sin/cos/sqrt/rsqrt). If that total exceeds 57 the compiler squeezes: it first sheds __KERN_0 (table folded into __TEXT), then packs every non-surface __data section into ONE shared segment and every __const section into ONE shared segment. A state surface is never packed. So nsegs = N+K+IN+OUT+2 (+1 with a kernel segment) when that is <= 57, else N+4 (N+3 when there is no data section besides the surfaces); compilation fails iff the squeezed total is still > 57, i.e. N >= 54 for any program with an output and N >= 55 with none. 53 = 55 - 2 shared segments. Why the pool is 55 ids (hardware BAR registers?) is not determined.
laws.domain: h17 and h16g (identical on both: N=3 IN=49/50, N=26 OUT=2/3, N=10/27/53 checked); rsw and read-only states; shapes 4x4 and mixed 4x4+64x32; fp16 io. Kernel-segment accounting verified only for IN=46..50 at N=3 and N=52/53/54 (tentative in detail).
laws.measurements: Predicted-vs-observed LC_SEGMENT_64 count: 112 gen_states_shape points (N in {0,1,5,10,20,26,27} at totals 55..59 plus 25 random, N<=53) and 132 gen_states_ops points (src=x0, K varied, targeted at totals 56..58 and N in {5,20,30,40,52,53}): 0 mismatches (5 N=0/IN>=52 points are invalid programs: dead u-chain -> CompilationFailure). Packing triggers at exactly 58 on three independent axes: inputs (N=3: IN=49 -> 57 segments unpacked, IN=50 -> 7), outputs (N=0: OUT=54 -> 57, OUT=55 -> 4; N=26: OUT=2 -> 57, OUT=3 -> 30) and the kernel segment (N=3 + sigmoid: IN=47 -> 57 with __KERN_0, IN=48 -> __KERN_0 shed, IN=49 -> packed). Squeezed minimum is N+4 for IN/OUT up to 100/100 and any sizes (60 outputs of 4..16384 elements all pack into one segment). Mixed-shape test: singles are exactly the N surfaces (15 x 0x400 + 15 x 0x20000 for 15+15 states) and the packed segment holds the other sections (copy-out sizes + outputs). N=52 + sigmoid: 54 FVMLIB + __KERN_0 + 2 = 57; N=53 + sigmoid: 55 FVMLIB, no __KERN_0, 57, runs rc 0; N=54 + sigmoid fails. Falsifier confirmed: 54 states with no output compile (54 surfaces + const + 2 = 57). Hypotheses: (a) BAR-id range: slot-word ordinals are exactly the FVMLIB segment indices (SLOT-WORD-BAR-ORDINAL), max 54 at N=53, 54 states would need ordinal 55 (supported, same quantity as the segment count). (b) 'data-bearing segments = N+1 <= 54': refuted as the budgeted quantity (const segments trigger the same packing: 3 states, 6 data segments, 49 inputs hits 57; 26 states unpacked have 54 data-bearing segments; a no-output program has 54 surfaces) - coincides with 'total FVMLIB <= 55' only after packing. (c) read-only state, dim0=1 (2x 0x9361), dim1=1/16, partial exposure: no effect on the cap.
laws.replaces_old_claim: 'Each state<> costs two __data segments (persistent surface + read/update working buffer)': the second section is the copy-out buffer of an EXPOSED state (absent when the updated value is not a program output), and sections are not segments. 'Only the persistent state<> params consume BAR entries' / 'io ports do not consume BAR entries': inputs, outputs and kernel tables consume the same 57-segment budget until packed/shed.
laws.counterexamples_checked: No state-free program reaches the BAR failure (everything non-state packs into 2 segments), and no weighted (conv BLOBFILE) program could be compiled through `milc ane compile` (blob path unresolved; inline conv weights InvalidMILProgram), so whether a weight segment is an unsheddable consumer that lowers the state cap below 53 is untested.

laws.statement: Section economy of the compiled HWX: #__FVMLIB.__data sections = N + K + OUT (state surfaces + one copy-out buffer per EXPOSED state + plain outputs), #__FVMLIB.__const sections = IN (plain inputs), #0x9442 records = #data sections (each data section is the destination of exactly one task), #0x9365 records = K (copy-out tasks), #0x9361 records = N (gen_states.py family). The old '2 x states + outputs' holds only because the repo generators expose every state (K = N).
laws.domain: h17; src=x0 family (gen_states.py, gen_states_ops.py) and gen_states_shape.py; 4x4 states; N<=53.
laws.measurements: N=53 IN=1 OUT=1, expose K=0,1,26,53: data sections 54,55,80,107 = 53+K+1; 0x9365 = 0,1,26,53. N=10 K=0..10: 0x9365 = K, 0x9442 = 11+K. 68 held-out random (N,K,IN,OUT) points: 0x9365 == K and 0x9361 == N in all. gen_states_shape.py: __data = OUT + 2N, matches the earlier 10 programs.
laws.replaces_old_claim: '__data segments = outputs + 2 x states' as a per-state cost model (docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md).

laws.statement: On h17, for programs whose slice_update source is the raw first plain input (gen_states.py; gen_states_ops.py src=x0): #0x9344 = K + max(1, min(IN, OUT)) for N >= 1, and = min(IN, OUT) for N = 0 (OUT >= 1), where K = number of states whose updated value is listed as a program output. Each exposed state adds exactly one 0x9344 (the primary-source binding of its copy-out task 0x9365, whose source is the state surface); an un-exposed state adds none. min(IN,OUT) is the number of distinct input-rooted output streams (outputs y_j = add(x_{j%IN}, x_{j%IN}) repeat and collapse when OUT > IN; inputs beyond OUT are dead); the update-source load shares the x0 stream, so the term is >= 1. The repo generators expose every state, so K = N and the count looks like 'N + const'; it is not a state count and not a cap.
laws.domain: h17; src=x0 update source; 4x4 states; 0 <= N <= 53; 0 <= K <= N; IN in [1,40]; OUT in [0,40]; rsw states. The computed-update-source generator gen_states_shape.py is a different, only partly modelled family (R9344-INTERCEPT-DRIFT).
laws.measurements: 56 held-out random gen_states.py (N,IN,OUT) points (+ specials (53,32,32)=85, (53,3,7)=56, (26,40,40)=66): predicted N+max(1,min(IN,OUT)) (OUT>=1) or N+1 (OUT=0) matched exactly, 0 mismatches. 68 held-out (N,K,IN,OUT) points with gen_g expose=K: 0x9344 == K+max(1,min(IN,OUT)), 0 mismatches. Additivity scans: 9344-K is constant over N in {0,1,2,3,4,10,26,27,28,40,52,53} for gen_states(1,1) (=1), gen_states(32,32) (=32), src=x0 IN4/OUT0 (=1), IN4/OUT3 (=3), src=x2 IN4/OUT3 (=3), chains=3 mul len3 (=3), chains=3 relu (=3). Direct: N=53 K=0 -> 1 record, K=1 -> 2, K=26 -> 27, K=53 -> 54; N=10 K=0..10 -> 1..11. Largest observed at 53 states: 119 (64 in/64 out). Task structure (in-order tag dump): compute task = 0x9342 0x935a [0x9344 src0] [0x934a src1..] [0x9442 dst]; copy-out task = 0x9365 [0x9344 state surface] [0x9442 out buffer]; state-write task = 0x9361 [0x9344 only if its source is not already bound] [0x9442 state surface].
laws.replaces_old_claim: '0x9344 = states + 1 header; the table holds 54 records' (docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md, count_desc_records.py header, spec lines 'records: 54 = the table cap'); 'the +1 header is present only when at least one state exists' (N=0 already has 1 record).

laws.statement: 0x9344 is not a layer/op/task count (hypothesis H-layers refuted): independent elementwise chains each rooted at their OWN plain input cost one record each regardless of chain length and op kind; a chain rooted at the input that already feeds the state update adds none (it merges with the update-source load); identical outputs collapse; __text length grows with ops but 0x9344 does not. The compile output exposes no layer/task count (only 'ModelMaxDramUsage = N'); `milc ane decompile --detail` recognises only elementwise tasks (reports '1 op' for a 2-state program).
laws.domain: h17; fp16 [1,4,1,1] tensors; elementwise add, mul, sub, maximum, relu, sigmoid, tanh, exp, abs, sqrt, square, softmax, reduce_sum chains (rsqrt rejected by the frontend); N=0 and N=3/10 with src=x0.
laws.measurements: N=0, C independent chains (own input each), 12 ops x C in {1,2,4} x len in {1,3}: 0x9344 == C in all 72 cells; chains of add with len 1,2,3,4,8 and C in {1,2,4,8}: == C. Single chain add / add,add / add,relu,mul: 1 record each while __text grows 0x13c -> 0x1bc -> 0x1cc; add,softmax,add: 1 record, __text 0x524. N=3 src=x0: chain add/add,add/add,relu,mul/softmax/add,softmax,add rooted at x0 -> 4 = N+1 (no change); reduce_sum rooted at x0 -> 5 (its [1,1,1,1] stream is a separate source load). N=10 mul chain len 8 -> 11 = 10+1. Update source on x_k vs output roots: N=3 IN=4, src=x0/OUT=1 -> 4, src=x1/OUT=1 -> 5, src=x3/OUT=2 -> 6 (merge only when roots coincide).
laws.replaces_old_claim: Hypothesis H-layers: 0x9344 = (#states) + (#compiled non-state layers/tasks).

laws.statement: When the update source is a computed tensor (gen_states_shape.py: u = x0+...+x{IN-1}), the non-state part of 0x9344 is C = 1 + max(1, min(IN,OUT)) for N >= 2 (N = 1: max(1,min(IN,OUT)), the producer fuses into its single consumer), but it grows by +1 at a program-dependent N* where a second compute task appears (0x9342/0x935a count rises 2 -> 3). So 0x9344 - N is NOT constant in N for this family (gen_states_shape.py 53 4 4 1 1 -> 55, not N+1 = 54). The u add-chain also splits in two at IN >= 98 (about 196 0x934a records in one task).
laws.domain: h17; gen_states_shape.py family; 4x4 / 64x32 states; observed thresholds only.
laws.measurements: Scan N=1..53: IN=OUT=32: C=32 (N=1), 33 (N=2..20), 34 (N>=21). IN=20/OUT=20: 21 -> 22 at N=33. IN=10/OUT=5: 6 -> 7 at N=45. IN=5/OUT=3: 4 -> 5 at N=49 (0x9342: 2 -> 3). IN=4/OUT=2: 3 -> 4 at N=50. IN=2/OUT=2 (4x4 and 64x32): 3 -> 4 at N=51. IN=2/OUT=40: 3 -> 4 at N=41 -> 5 at N=51. IN=1/OUT=1, IN<=3/OUT<=1, IN=1/OUT=60, IN=20/OUT=0: no bump up to 53. N=3 OUT=2: C=3 for IN<=97, 4 for IN>=98. Bump positions fit 2N+IN+OUT ~ 105-106 for the OUT>=2 families but not for the others, so the real trigger (a per-task descriptor-list capacity) is not identified.
laws.replaces_old_claim: '0x9344 = N+1 for N states' for any generator other than the single-input gen_states.py.

laws.statement: Every 0x9344 / 0x934a / 0x9442 record is a 12-byte buffer binding: [tag u16][bar_word u16][offset u32][0 u32], with bar_word = (0x46 + ordinal) << 7 = 0x2300 + 0x80*ordinal (equivalently (slot_index<<8)|(copy<<7) with slot_index = 0x23 + ordinal//2, copy = ordinal&1) where ordinal is the 0-based index of the target __FVMLIB segment in LC_SEGMENT_64 order (__PAGEZERO excluded), and offset = section.addr - segment.vmaddr of a section inside that segment (0 for single-section segments; multiples of the section pitch in packed segments). 0x9344 = a task's primary source, 0x934a = further sources, 0x9442 = destination. Every FVMLIB segment is referenced (distinct ordinals == #FVMLIB), max ordinal seen 54 (word 0x3e00). For gen_states.py (IN=OUT=1) the 0x9344 ordinals are {0..N-1} (state surfaces) plus the input-segment ordinal h: h = 2N for N <= 26 (unpacked layout: surfaces 0..N-1, copy-out buffers N..2N-1, then const; ordinals N..2N-1 get no 0x9344) and h = N+1 for 27 <= N <= 53 (packed layout: surfaces, one packed data segment at ordinal N, const at N+1; ordinal N never appears in 0x9344). The old 'header k = N+1, k = N unused' holds only in the packed regime N >= 27.
laws.domain: h17 and h16g (identical decode, checked on 7 programs); all 896 artifacts compiled in this unit (rsw, read-only, mixed shapes, kernel segments, 0..100 plain inputs). Exception to the sub-claim '0x934a addresses a __const segment': operands that are intermediate tensors address a data segment (2 artifacts with a producer op before the update).
laws.measurements: 896 artifacts, 83,087 records: 0 violations of tag/bar_word/offset/zero layout and ordinal < #FVMLIB. N sweep 0..53 (gen_states.py 1/1): records = N+1 always; sorted 0x9344 ordinals = {0..N-1} + {h}; first/header ordinal = 2N for N=0..26 (0,2,4,...,52), = N+1 for N=27..53 (28..54); missing ordinals = N..2N-1 (unpacked) or {N} (packed). Specific: N=0 -> ordinals {0}, 9442 on ordinal 1; N=1 -> {0,2}; N=2 -> {0,1,4}; N=27 -> {0..26,28}; N=52 -> {0..51,53}; N=53 -> {0..52,54}, bar_word max 0x3e00. 53 states + 32 in + 32 out: 85 records but still 55 ordinals.
laws.replaces_old_claim: 'word = (slot_index<<8)|(copy<<7) where slot_index is a descriptor-table slot holding up to two records' (a BAR/segment id, not a table slot); 'slot word bit layout undecoded'; prior brief 'k = 0..N-1 states, header k = N+1' for all N.

laws.statement: A compiled state program executes iff (IN + N) + (OUT + K) <= 127: each declared state is one input port, each exposed state output (updated value listed in the program outputs) is one output port; otherwise execute_sync fails with ANEProgramProcessRequestDirect status=0x2 'Program Inference error' (milc exit 1, 'step 0: execute_sync -> 11'). With plain ports this is the live_in + out <= 127 law of the port unit. Consequences: with all 53 states exposed only IN+OUT <= 21 remain, so gen_states.py 53 32 32 compiles (85 records) but does not run; with no exposed states a state costs one port (53 states leave IN+OUT <= 73).
laws.domain: h17 hardware (M5 Max); gen_states_shape.py, gen_states_ops.py src=x0 expose=K, gen_g; N<=53; all inputs live.
laws.measurements: Boundary at 127/128 on 17 distinct (N,IN,OUT,K) points, each run twice, zero flips: N=53 K=53: (10,11) ok, (11,11) fail, (1,20) ok, (1,21) fail, (20,1) ok, (21,1) fail; N=40 K=40: (23,24) ok, (24,24) fail, (1,46) ok, (1,47) fail; N=53 K=0: OUT=73 ok / 74 fail; N=53 K=26: OUT=47 ok / 48 fail; N=10 K=0: OUT=116 ok / 117 fail; N=10 K=10: OUT=106 ok / 107 fail; N=1: (1,124) ok, (1,125) fail, (63,62) ok, (63,63) fail; N=0: (1,126) ok / (1,127) fail, (63,64) ok / (64,64) fail. 53 states, 1/1: rc 0 for all shapes with d0*d1 <= 256.
laws.replaces_old_claim: Old spec 'step 0:' regex assertions that also matched the failure line; the implicit reading that compile-clean 53-state programs with 32 in/32 out are usable.

laws.statement: A state<tensor<fp16,[d0,d1,1,1]>> only executes if d0*d1 <= 256 (512 bytes, independent of the d0/d1 split); larger states compile (up to 53 x 64x32) but execution fails with status=0x1d 'Program Inference error', even for a single state. Non-state tensors of 4096 elements run, so the limit is specific to state surfaces. 53 states of 256 elements each run.
laws.domain: h17 hardware; fp16 [d0,d1,1,1] rsw states, update row [1,d1,1,1]; shape arrangement independent over 31 shapes; dtype/rank not varied.
laws.replaces_old_claim: Implicit 'state width (rows/state 4 -> 256) is irrelevant' (spec lines on gen_states_width.py), which only holds for compile.

laws.statement: The ANE frontend (`milc ane validate`/compile validation) rejects a program once declared in+out >= 256 with MaxLiveInLiveOutExceeded; each state counts as one input and each exposed state as one output, so with all states exposed and 1 plain in/out N <= 126 passes and N >= 127 fails. A program with zero plain inputs is rejected (InvalidMILProgram), so a shared __const segment always exists. This frontend limit is independent of, and above, the compile-time BAR cap (N <= 53).
laws.domain: h17 and h16g validate; gen_states_shape.py N 4 4 1 1.
laws.measurements: validate N=53,54,55,100,125,126: rc 0 'status=0x0 rc=0'; N=127,128,200: rc 1 MaxLiveInLiveOutExceeded (x2). h16g validate 53,54: rc 0. IN=0 programs: InvalidMILProgram (status 0x1) at N=0,1,53,54.
laws.replaces_old_claim: 'Finding 2: the state<> limit IS a frontend constraint' (it is an ANECCompile constraint; the frontend validates 54..126 states).

open_questions: Why exactly 55 ids (57 LC_SEGMENT_64)? The pool size is read off the output Mach-O; no allocator source or register documentation was available. Candidates: 64 BAR registers minus 9 reserved, or minus 7 with PAGEZERO/TEXT inside the pool. Not separable by any lever found, because everything except state surfaces packs or sheds.

Is any non-state consumer unpackable and unsheddable (weights/conv BLOBFILE, multi-function, large tensors)? If a weight segment costs a BAR, the practical state cap for real models is below 53. Weighted programs could not be compiled here: `milc ane compile` of a .mil with BLOBFILE fails 'Cannot retrieve file blob properties' even with a sibling weights/ dir, and inline conv weights are InvalidMILProgram.

When __KERN_0 is shed at the 57 boundary (53 states + sigmoid/softmax), the table is folded into __TEXT (__const 0x4000 -> 0x80, file size changes). It runs (rc 0) but numerical equivalence with the 52-state variant was not checked (milc ane run prints only timing).

R9344-INTERCEPT-DRIFT: the trigger of the extra compute task at high N for computed update sources (N*=21 for 32/32, 33 for 20/20, 45 for 10/5, 49 for 5/3, 50 for 4/2, 51 for 2/2) and the split of the u add chain at IN>=98 are unmodelled; a per-task descriptor-list capacity (~196 0x934a records) is the likely cause.

STATE-RUN-SIZE-256: is the limit 256 elements or 512 bytes (only fp16 states exist here), and does it depend on rank (only [d0,d1,1,1] tried), on the slice_update row, or on the arch? status=0x1d is undecoded. 4D states such as [1,H,S,D] KV-caches were not tried and are the real use case for Chimera.

Do multiple writes to one state, cross-state copies (slice from state i into state j), or a state read in the middle of a graph change the segment cost or the 0x9344/0x9365 task structure? Only the read -> slice_update(plain input) -> write_state triple was generated.
h16g facts (cap, packing threshold, slot decode) are cross-compiles on the M5 host only; nothing was loaded or run on M4 hardware, and h16g run-time limits (ports, state size) are unmeasured.

Zero-output programs compile but the E5 bundle fails to load ('op_create -> 13', also at N=1): the loader requirement (>=1 output?) is not characterised, so the 54/55 compile boundary for output-less programs has no runtime meaning yet.

The per-state 0x9361/0x9365 body fields (dim1 at +0x0a etc.) were out of scope for this unit; the earlier 'read record is a fixed template' and stride-law corrections belong to the record-layout unit.
notes:
Ground truth for the state<> budget, re-measured on Apple M5 Max (h17), macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), milc built at vendor/mil_spec/target/release/milc. Nothing under the repo worktree was modified (git status clean; no commit, push, stash or checkout). All work is under WD=<wd>/re/state/ (drivers drv.py/pt/runspec.py, generators gen_g.py/gen_seq.py/gen_kern.py/gen_mixshape.py, analyzers mx.py/seq.py/segmap.py/ordcheck.py/offcheck.py/segpred*.py/pred*.py, proposed/*.py, proposed.spec, results.jsonl, spec_results.json). Compiles do not touch the ANE; about 150 ANE runs were serial, every boundary point was executed twice and none flipped (the 61 proposed assertions were each executed twice via an emulation of the harness: sh -c from repo root, @T@ -> WD/spec/, 0 failing, 0 flips). Because the user wants the repo kept current on GitHub: the orchestrator must add the three scripts and the spec edits; this unit did not push.

HEADLINE: (1) 53/54 is real and robust, but it is a SEGMENT budget, not a state-count or 0x9344 table: the Mach-O may hold 57 LC_SEGMENT_64 (55 __FVMLIB/__KERN_* + __PAGEZERO + __TEXT), state surfaces are the only buffers that never pack, so N+4 <= 57. A program with no outputs compiles 54 states (compile-only; it does not load). 55 ids, not 54 records. (2) 0x9344 is not a cap and not a layer count: it is K (states whose updated value is a program output) + the number of distinct input-rooted source streams; 53 states with nothing exposed have ONE 0x9344 record yet 54 still fail. The old 'records=54 slots=28 fullcopies=26' output of decode_slot_word.py stays numerically true for gen_states.py 53 1 1 but 'slot' there is just a pair of consecutive BAR ordinals. (3) The slot word is a BAR/segment id: (0x46+ordinal)<<7; the 12-byte record also carries the section offset inside the segment. (4) A compile-clean 53-state program is not necessarily runnable: ports (IN+N)+(OUT+K) <= 127 (status 0x2) and per-state size d0*d1 <= 256 fp16 elements (status 0x1d); gen_states.py 53 32 32 compiles but fails to run, which the old vacuous 'step 0:' regex assertions could not have caught.

SPEC EDIT GUIDANCE: replace the 'descriptor economy' prose and the count_desc_records.py/decode_slot_word.py header text accordingly; every pass-side run assertion must use want_rc 0 (and want_out_re '^step 0: [0-9]'); keep the existing 53/54 compile lines (still true) and add the proposed ones. The harness semantics I assumed: want_out substring, want_out_re re.search with MULTILINE (so ^step 0: works), want_absent substring-absent, want_rc compares the exit code of the last command of the run line. The new scripts need require_file lines. Existing scripts count_desc_records.py / decode_9365.py / decode_slot_word.py parse section_64 correctly now and were used unchanged (count_desc_records agreed with decode_slot_ordinals records= on every assertion).

PITFALLS FOUND: (a) milc prints no layer/task count at compile, only 'ModelMaxDramUsage = N'; `milc ane decompile --detail` lists just elementwise tasks. (b) A plain input is mandatory (InvalidMILProgram otherwise); dead u-chains / dead inputs give CompilationFailure (gen_states_shape.py 0 ... IN>1 does not compile). (c) gen_states.py and gen_states_shape.py are different 0x9344 families (raw vs computed update source); do not extrapolate counts between them. (d) slice_update without write_state and constant update sources are rejected; read-only states (read_state only) are accepted. (e) Kernel (LUT) ops add a __KERN_0 segment that is silently shed at the budget edge. (f) State execution has two independent failure statuses: 0x2 (ports) and 0x1d (state > 256 elements); zero-output programs fail to load. (g) h16g results are cross-compile only. For Chimera.Next scheduling: plan at most 53 persistent state tensors per compiled program (52 when a weight/other unpackable segment is later found to cost one), each <= 256 fp16 elements, and count states as ports ((IN+N)+(OUT+K) <= 127); expose only the states you must read back.

laws.statement: Every state-copy record in __TEXT.__text is framed by the u16 0x8005 immediately followed by a tag from the 8-value family {0x9260,0x9261,0x9264,0x9265,0x9360,0x9361,0x9364,0x9365}. tag = 0x9261 + 0x100*[dim1!=1] + 0x004*[dim0!=1] - 0x001*[dim1==16]. The low bits are presence flags of an elided-default field list: bit0 = dim1 field present (default 16), bit2 = dim0 field present (default 1), bit8 = stride word present (default 0, i.e. dim1==1). The tag is a pure function of (dim0,dim1): independent of N, plain in/out port counts, update mode (plain-input vs add-chain), dim2, and arch (h17 and h16g identical). dim0==1 vs >=2 is the only dim0 breakpoint; dim1==1 and dim1==16 are the only dim1 special values. Exception: dim3 == 256 (any d0,d1,d2) emits NO copy record at all (program still executes and updates the state).
laws.domain: fp16 states only (all other state dtypes fail to compile). Compiled for h17 and h16g on the M5 Max host. N in {1,2,3,4,10,53}; dim0 in {1,2,3,4,5,7,8,16,17,64,100,1000}; dim1 in 1..80 plus 96..4095; dim2<=16 and dim3 spot-checked (tag independent of both); both update modes (add-chain gen_states_shape.py, plain-input gen_states.py/width).
laws.measurements: 539-point grid (11 dim0 x 49 dim1, N=1): exactly one copy record per program and tag == formula at 539/539. Requested grid dim0{1,2,4,8,64} x dim1{1..10,12,15,16,17,24,31,32,33,48,63,64,65,128,256} at N=1: dim1==1 -> 0x9261 (dim0=1) / 0x9265; dim1==16 -> 0x9360 / 0x9364; every other dim1 -> 0x9361 / 0x9365. Earlier tag counting that only looked at 0x9360/61/64/65 missed the 0x926x sub-family, hence the false 'dim1==1 -> none'. N=2,3,53: same tag for every record of the program (dim0>1: 0x936x/0x926x mix of dim0-less + dim0 tags; dim0==1: all records dim0-less). Battery of 1184 + 750 programs decoded with zero tag/field mismatches. dim3 scan 1..1100 and 256*k to 16384 (+ 960 (d0,d1,d2,d3) combos): copy family absent iff dim3==256. Same byte-for-byte tag choice on --arch h16g.
laws.counterexamples_checked: dim1 = 15,17,32,64,128,256,1024 (not special); dim1==16 with dim2=16 or dim3=16 still 0x9364 (so not row-element-count dim1*dim2*dim3==16); dim1==1 with dim3=16 stays 0x926x. dtype cannot be varied (only fp16 states compile) so '16 elements' vs '32 bytes' is NOT separable. dim3==256 is the only value in 1..1100 that drops the family.
laws.replaces_old_claim: 'dim1==1 gives no copy records at all' (review A12); implicit 'one fixed 0x9361/0x9365 pair for every shape'.

laws.statement: There are two record ROLES (not 'read-side/write-side'). (a) UPDATE-ROW copy ([1,dim1(,dim2,dim3)] update row -> state): one per state, except that the first state has none when the slice_update source is an add-chain computed on the ANE (gen_states_shape.py: N-1 records); N records when the source is a plain input (gen_states.py, gen_states_width.py). (b) STATE-OUT copy (full [dim0,dim1] updated tensor -> output port, tag with the dim0 field when dim0>1): one per state-update tensor that is ALSO a program output (every repo generator returns all upd_i, so N). With dim0==1 the dim0 field is elided so both roles carry the dim0-less tag: total 2N (plain-input) or 2N-1 (add-chain). Ordering in the stream is R W R W ... (add-chain: the first W has an R before it, the last W has none).
laws.domain: fp16 states, dim2=dim3=1, N in {1,2,3,4,10,53}, both update modes, ports (in,out) up to (32,32). Returned-subset test at N=4: all / none / only upd0 / only upd3 / upd1+upd2.
laws.measurements: gen_states_shape.py: N=1:(R=0,W=1) N=2:(1,2) N=3:(2,3) N=4:(3,4) N=10:(9,10) N=53:(52,53) for dim0>1; gen_states.py N=1..4,10,53: (N,N). With upd outputs not returned (noupd) N=4 gives W=0 in both modes, R unchanged (3 add-chain / 4 plain-input); returning only upd0 or only upd3 gives W=1; upd1+upd2 gives W=2. dim0==1: gen_states_shape N=1,2,3,53 -> 1,3,5,105 records (all 0x9361); gen_states.py N=1,2,3,53 -> 2,4,6,106.
laws.counterexamples_checked: Counts independent of plain in/out counts (ni,no in 1..5) and of dims (battery). Building the update source with a const (IN=0) is rejected by ANECCompile (InvalidMILProgram) so that path cannot be tested.
laws.replaces_old_claim: '0x9361 = read-side, 0x9365 = write-side, one of each per state'; the H56 'read/write asymmetry' framing.

laws.statement: The stride word of every copy record (u32 located 0x0a bytes after the constant 0x00014000 header word: +0x1c in 0x9365, +0x18 in 0x9361/0x9364, +0x14 in 0x9360, absent in 0x926x) is 8*min(ceil(log2(dim1)),4) for dim2=dim3=1: dim1=1->0 (field elided), 2->8, 3-4->16, 5-8->24, >=9->32 (saturated). It is independent of dim0 and N, identical in update-row and state-out records, and identical on h16g. Equivalent form in row bytes b=2*dim1: 8*min(ceil(log2 b)-1,4).
laws.measurements: dim1 sweep at dim0=4: stride 8,16,16,24,24,24,24,32,... exactly as stated, saturated through 4096. dim0 in {2,3,8,64,1000}: unchanged. 1184-program battery: decoded stride == 8*min(ceil(log2 dim1),4) in every record. h16g: dim1=2,5,9 -> 8,24,32. Old law min(2*dim1+8,32) gives 10,12,14,18,20,22,26 at dim1=1,2,3,5,6,7,9 and agrees only at dim1=4,8 and >=12.
laws.counterexamples_checked: Row-size/dtype dependence cannot be separated (fp16 only). With dim2>1 the word changes (see copy-header-dim23), so this law is scoped to dim2=1.
laws.replaces_old_claim: stride = min(2*dim1+8, 32) (spec/handoff H55).

laws.statement: Record header (byte offsets from the tag; all fields LE u32 at 2-byte alignment): +0x02 dim3, +0x06 dim2, +0x0a dim1 (if tag bit0), then dim0 (if tag bit2), then the constant 0x00014000 (=81920), then dim2 again, stride word 0x0a after the 0x14000 word. The '1' constants at +0x02/+0x06 in every dim2=dim3=1 record are dim3 and dim2. dim2>1 or dim3>1 is ACCEPTED by compile and runs ([4,4,2,1], [4,4,1,2] rc=0). Effects: dim2>1 makes the state-out record 8 bytes longer (core 0x86 vs 0x7e) and adds ceil(log2 dim2)-ish bits to the stride word (d1=4: dim2=1,2,3,4,5-8,9-16 -> 16,17,18,18,19,20; for dim1>=5 dim2=2 already adds 2); dim3>1 leaves the stride word alone but scales the rowbits fields: rowbits = 16*dim1*ceil(dim3/8) for dim3<=128, saturating beyond (d1=4: 2048, d1=11: 2816). These derived-field sub-laws are tentative; the header positions are strong.
laws.domain: fp16; dim2 in {1..16,31..1000 compile-only}; dim3 in 1..4096; dim2>=17 changes the layout further (stride field read at the old offset is garbage, e.g. 1048596) and is not decoded.
laws.counterexamples_checked: Tag bits are independent of dim2/dim3 ((4,1,16,1),(4,1,1,16),(4,4,4,1) keep the dim1-derived tag). Execution of dim2/dim3>1 states follows the state-exec-pages rule.
laws.replaces_old_claim: Implicit assumption that the +0x02/+0x06 words are constants and that only dim0/dim1 vary.

laws.statement: A state-out record has two layouts selected by the word after the 0x1041 marker: SHORT (0x1041 0x803c 0x0142 ...) and LONG (0x1041 0x803e 0x0162 ..., 4 bytes longer: one extra leading rowbits u32 before the 0x0010 constant, and the final 0x014a field is 2*rowbits=32*dim1 instead of rowbits). rowbits = the u16 that appears three times just before the 0x9052 tag = 16*dim1 mod 2^16 (row width in fp16 bits); REGION = rowbits<<16 = dim1 MiB mod 4 GiB (wraps to 0 at dim1=4096). The old reading u32@+0x48 equals dim1 MiB only in SHORT records; in LONG records +0x48 is the constant 1 MiB and dim1 MiB sits at +0x44. FORM RULE: in programs whose update source is a plain input (gen_states.py, gen_states_width.py) exactly the LAST state-out record (stream order) is SHORT and all earlier ones LONG, for any N and any port counts (N=1: the single record is SHORT). In add-chain programs (gen_states_shape.py) the number of trailing SHORT records depends on N and ports: 2 when in==1 or out==1 (N>=2), otherwise 1 for small port counts falling to 0 as N and ports grow (N>=8 with in,out>=2: all LONG); a W directly followed by the 0x9640 footer is always SHORT; no closed form found.
laws.domain: fp16 states, dim2=dim3=1, dim0>=2, N=1..53, ports up to (32,32), h17 (h16g decodes identically).
laws.measurements: Standard 53-state program (gen_states.py 53 1 1): 52 LONG + 1 SHORT, all dim0=4 dim1=4 stride=16 region=4194304 (old decode_9365.py prints region=1048576 because it reads +0x48 of the first, LONG, record). Plain-input mode: forms = L^(N-1) S for N=1..10 and 53, ports (1,1),(5,5),(1,5),(5,1),(2,2),(32,32) (verified across 18 dims each). Add-chain, ni=no=1: N=2 SS, N=3 LSS, N=4 LLSS, N=5 LLLSS, N=6 LLLLSS, N=8 LL..LSS. Add-chain S-count matrix: N=3: ni>=2,no>=2 -> 1 (0 at ni=4-6,no=8 and ni>=7,no>=7); N=5: ni=2: 1 for no<=6, ni=3,4: no<=5, ni>=5: no<=4, else 0; N=6: ni=2,3: no<=4, ni>=4: no<=3, else 0; N=8,10: 0 for all ni,no in 2..8. (5,5,N=5) and (32,32,N=2) are all-LONG. Extra LONG variant when in,out>=2: first u16 of the record carries an additive offset (flags 0x803e 0x0142, e.g. 352 for (2,2),d1=11) but the triple before 0x9052 stays 16*dim1. Executing every variant is fine (dim0/dim1/dim5 family runs rc=0).
laws.counterexamples_checked: Local-context test: a state-out record followed by the 0x9640 footer was SHORT in 34/34 cases, but a record followed by a 0x9344 list is either form (99 LONG / 21 SHORT), so no local rule. Text size, #0x9344, #0x934a, port sum are not separating features (no linear threshold fits the 245 add-chain cases).
laws.replaces_old_claim: '0x9365 region = dim1 MiB for single-state/last record, 1 MiB for the others' as a universal record-index rule (true only for plain-input programs); decode_9365.py region on the standard program.

laws.statement: The update-row record (0x9361 family without the dim0 field) is NOT a fixed template. Field map (offsets from the tag): +0x02 dim3, +0x06 dim2, +0x0a dim1 (if tag bit0), +0x0e 0x00014000 (shifts -4 when dim1==16), +0x12 dim2 repeat, +0x18 stride word (absent when dim1==1), +0x20 const 0x0020, then the form-specific body. Forms by marker flags: COMPACT (core 0x4a bytes: 1045 9800 0010 0000 014a 0000 <rowbits@+0x2e> 0000 1241 8002 3c0c 0010 3c00 0000 1445 8080 0040 0000 2031 0130), FIRST (plain-input programs, core 0x52: 1041 8004 0100 0010 0010 0000 9052 0000 014a 0040 <rowbits@+0x36> ...; flags 0x0000 when dim1==1) and SHORT (add-chain first update-row, core 0x72: 1342 8008 00ee ... 1041 803c 0141 0010 0010 0000 R 0000 R 0000 R 0000 9052 0000 014a 0040 R ...). The first update-row of a plain-input program is FIRST, all others COMPACT; the first (and only non-COMPACT) of an add-chain program is SHORT. The core depends on dim1 (+0x0a, stride, 16*dim1 words) and not on dim0; the embedded 0x9442 child (starts right after the core, slot word at child+2) carries a per-record slot word (plain-input N=4: 0x2380,0x2400,0x2300,0x2480) and a running record index. The record is 0xa0 bytes long from its 0x8005 frame to the next frame (COMPACT/FIRST), 0xd0 for the add-chain SHORT first one, 0xa8 for the last plain-input one.
laws.domain: fp16, dim2=dim3=1, h17 (h16g same layout), N=2..53, both modes.
laws.measurements: dim1=4 vs 8 add-chain N=2/3: cores differ (dim1 and stride 16 vs 24 and 64 vs 128 rowbits); framed-record byte diff across dim0 in {2,3,7,64,1000}: only the cost word (see copy-update-row-cost) differs for dim0>=31, the core is identical (digest equality asserted). Old cmp_9361.py passes on gen_states_width (varies dim0 only) and reports 'bodies differ' on dim1=4 vs 8.
laws.counterexamples_checked: dim0==1 programs: update-row and state-out both appear as dim0-less tags (forms short/long) and cannot be separated by tag alone.
laws.replaces_old_claim: '0x9361 is a fixed template; only 0x9365 carries the shape' (H56, cmp_9361.py as evidence).

laws.statement: In every COMPACT update-row record the u16 following the 0x0038 word of the embedded 0x9442 child (tag+0x6e) equals floor(dim0*dim1*2 / K) with K=450 on h17 and K=534 on h16g (state bytes divided by a per-arch constant: looks like a compiler DMA-time/cost estimate; units unknown). It is the only dim0-dependent byte outside the state-out header.
laws.domain: fp16, dim2=dim3=1, dim0>=2, dim1 not in {1,16}-special offsets handled by anchoring on the 0x0038 word; compact records except the last update-row of a plain-input program (which has a 0x0040 variant).
laws.measurements: h17: 130+ (dim0,dim1) points, e.g. (1000,11)->48, (1000,22)->97, (4096,2)->36, (65536,11)->3203, (2000,10)->88; feasible K interval fitted from 60 points: (449.993, 450.000]. h16g: K interval (533.865, 534.010] from 60 points, e.g. (1000,11)->41. Independent of N, mode and ports (checked ports (2,2),(5,5)).
laws.counterexamples_checked: Last update-row of a plain-input program shows a different word after 0x0040 (not decoded). dim0==1 or dim1==1 records use shifted offsets; the decoder anchors on the child so reports '-' where the form differs.
laws.replaces_old_claim: '0x9361 ignores dim0' (true for the core, false for this trailing field).

laws.statement: Records are self-framed: 0x8005 <tag> ... up to the next 0x8005 (or the 0x9640 footer region). Core = tag .. end of the 0x2031 0x0130 pair: COMPACT update-row 0x4a, FIRST 0x52, SHORT update-row 0x72, state-out SHORT 0x7e, state-out LONG 0x82 (dim2=dim3=1). Typical framed lengths: update-row 0xa0, LONG state-out 0xe0, non-last SHORT 0xe8, last state-out 0xc4.
laws.measurements: 0x8005 precedes the family tag in 79/79 random programs; the same prefix precedes the 0x9541 (0x9540 when dim1==16) compute records.
laws.counterexamples_checked: none needed beyond the battery.
laws.replaces_old_claim: decode scripts that counted bare 2-byte tag matches without framing.

laws.statement: An fp16 ANE state<tensor<fp16,[d0,d1,d2,d3]>> compiles but only EXECUTES (execute_sync ok) iff ceil(true_bytes/16384) == ceil(padded_bytes/16384), where rows = d0*d1*d2, true_bytes = rows*d3*2 and padded_bytes = rows*64*ceil(2*d3/64) (rows laid out with a 64 B stride). Otherwise ANEProgramProcessRequestDirect fails with status=0x1d 'Program Inference error' (milc exit code 1). Corollaries: d3 a multiple of 32 elements always executes (no padding), including very large states (e.g. [4,16,1,16384]); for d3<32 the state needs d0*d1*d2 <= 256 (one 16 KiB page of 64 B rows) with narrow escapes when padding does not change the page count (e.g. [1,300,1,31] passes, [1,260,1,31] fails). The rule is per state and independent of N, of whether upd outputs are returned and of the copy-record family; dim3 itself is uncapped (>= 16384 run).
laws.domain: fp16 states, N in {1,2,3,5,10,53}, d0 up to 300, d1 up to 8193, d2 up to 10, d3 1..16385; macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M5 Max (h17). Execution on M4 hardware not tested.
laws.measurements: Predictor (state_exec_predict.py rule) vs hardware on 187 random shapes (3 seeds, N in {1,2,3}) + ~40 hand-picked boundary points: 0 mismatches; every boundary point run twice (and (1,260,1,31)/(1,300,1,31) six times), no flips. Key points: [16,16]x2 pass, [16,17] fail, [8,32] pass/[8,33] fail, [1,256]/[1,257], [256,1]/[257,1], [128,2]/[129,2], [4,64] pass/[4,65] fail, N=53 [16,16] pass/[16,17] fail; with d3: [16,17,1,32] pass, [16,17,1,33] fail, [1,260,1,d3] passes for d3 in {28..32,55..64,96,127,128,160,192,256,512,1024} and fails for 1..27,33..54,65..69,97,100,129,257,1000; [1,d1,1,31] fails for d1=257..261 and 513, passes for 256,270..512,1000. Plain-IO programs without states ran at dim1=4096. Failing shapes pass ANECCompile (status=0x0 rc=0).
laws.counterexamples_checked: First hypotheses 'dim0*dim1 <= 256' and 'rows<=256 unless d3%32==0' were refuted by [1,300,1,31]/[1,1,300,31] (pass) vs [1,260,1,31]/[1,1,257,31] (fail); the page rule explains all of them. Not a plain-IO artifact: noupd and plain-input variants fail identically.
laws.replaces_old_claim: None stated explicitly; the repo's '53 states actually run' assertion only covered [4,4] states.

laws.statement: The 53-state ANECCompile limit ('unable to allocate free BAR' at 54) does not depend on the state-out copy records: with no state-update tensor returned as a program output (no 0x9365 at all) 53 states still compile and 54, 60, 100 states still fail with the BAR error, in both update modes.
laws.measurements: noupd direct/add: N=53 status=0x0; N=54,60,100 status=0x16 rc=22 'ZinBarIdManager::GetNextAvailableBarId(): unable to allocate free BAR' (process exit code 1).
laws.counterexamples_checked: Only h17 checked in this configuration.
laws.replaces_old_claim: Any reading of the 54-record/'table holds 54 records' story that ties the cap to the per-state copy-record count (here 53 states emit 52-53 update-row and 0 state-out records and still compile).

laws.statement: Two non-dimensional flag words in the first update-row record and the first LONG state-out record flip when dim1 (or dim2) reaches 511: first update-row (add-chain) word at +0x54 goes 0x0040 -> 0x0010 and first long state-out word at +0x60 goes 0x0000 -> 0x0040; the affine dim fields stay linear. Layout shifts again at dim1 >= 65535.
laws.domain: add-chain N=4, dim2=dim3=1, dim0 in {7,1000}; dim1 510 vs 511 (bisected 257..1000), dim2 511.
laws.measurements: bisect: 510 -> (0x40,0x00), 511 -> (0x10,0x40); (7,1,511,1) flips too; dim3=511 does not (different layout).
laws.counterexamples_checked: dim0 and dim3 do not move the threshold.
laws.replaces_old_claim: none

laws.statement: ANECCompile also rejects very large states (CompilationFailure) in a way that depends on rows (everything except W) and not on dim3: single state [1,x,1,1] fails above x=4194304 (2^22); [2,x,1,1] above 2796160; [65536,x,1,1] above x=127; [1000,x,1,d3] above x=8380 for d3 in {1,2,31,32} (N=1), 4192 (N=2), 2795 (N=3); [x,1,1,1] above 65536. W-axis-heavy states ([4,16,1,400000], [1,1,x,1024]) compile far past 16 MiB.
laws.measurements: bisections listed in the statement; pattern consistent with total (state+returned update+io) elements ~2^24 for d3=1 but not for d3=64 ([1,x,1,64] fails above 2^21), so the exact formula is unknown.
laws.counterexamples_checked: Not pursued; outside this unit's scope.
laws.replaces_old_claim: none

laws.statement: Only fp16 state tensors compile for the ANE path: fp32 states fail with CompilationFailure, int8/uint8/int16/bool states with InvalidMILProgram (int32 additionally lists invalid ops). Consequently dtype-byte-width hypotheses for the dim1==16 special case and the stride word cannot be tested. gen_states_shape.py with IN=0 (const update source, advertised in its comment) is also rejected (InvalidMILProgram) in both generator modes.
laws.domain: state dtype in {fp16,fp32,int8,uint8,int16,int32,bool}, shapes [4,{8,11,16,32}]; IN=0 shapes [4,4].
laws.measurements: 28 dtype/shape compiles: only fp16 status=0x0; direct-mode retest same.
laws.counterexamples_checked: none
laws.replaces_old_claim: gen_states_shape.py header comment 'a const when in == 0'.

open_questions: Is the dim1==16 special case about 16 elements or 32 bytes (= the saturated stride row)? Only fp16 states compile, so dtype cannot separate them. Same for the stride word's 'log2 of row bytes' form.

What determines SHORT vs LONG for state-out records in add-chain programs? Observed: a record directly before the 0x9640 footer is always SHORT, but in(1) or out(1) gives two trailing SHORTs, in,out>=2 gives one, large N/ports gives none, and no linear/size/count feature separates the 245 cases. Needs the compiler's task-splitting logic, not more sampling.

What are the constants 0x14000 (=81920), the 0x0038/0x0040 child words, the per-record running index (1,2,3,... odd for update-row, even for state-out) and the slot words (e.g. 0x2380,0x2400,0x2300,0x2480 for the 4-state plain-input program)? Slot allocation belongs to the 0x9344 unit.

What is the update-row 'cost' = floor(dim0*dim1*2/K) (K=450 h17, 534 h16g)? A compiler DMA-time/cost-model estimate is plausible (the per-arch constant suggests it) but units, consumers and whether the scheduler/firmware reads it are unknown. If it is a real model input it is a free cost oracle for Chimera.Next's scheduler.

state-exec-pages: the rule (padded size must not need more 16 KiB pages than the true size) fits 190+ random shapes, but the mechanism (compiler sizes the state buffer from unpadded bytes, hardware strides by 64 B) is inferred, not observed. Numerics of passing cases were only spot-checked (kv0 1024/4096 nonzero at dim3=256). Untested on M4 hardware and other macOS builds.

Compile-time state caps: single state [1,x,1,1] fails above x=2^22, [65536,x,1,1] above x=127, [1000,x,1,d3] above x=8380 for d3 in {1,2,31,32} but W-heavy states ([4,16,1,400000]) compile; pattern is rows-based but the exact formula (io tensors counted? 2^23-ish) is unknown. Belongs to a shape-limits unit.

dim2>1 stride-word law: +ceil(log2 dim2) for dim1<=4, but dim2=2 adds 2 when dim1>=5, and dim2>=17 changes the record layout (stride read at the old offset is garbage); rowbits for dim3>8 follow 16*dim1*ceil(dim3/8) only up to dim3~128 then saturate at dim1-dependent values (2048 at d1=4, 2816 at d1=11), and dim2=3,4 give rowbits 80 at d1=4. No closed form; the repo generators never emit dim2/dim3>1.
Why does dim3==256 (and only 256 among 1..1100, 256k to 16384 and 960 shape combos) remove all copy records? Probably the update row already matches the plain-IO layout; not confirmed.

Why do two flag words flip exactly at dim1 (or dim2) == 511 (9-bit saturation?) and is any behaviour (not only bytes) different there? Such shapes only execute if dim3 is a multiple of 32, so this was not probed on hardware.
The h16g (M4) results are cross-compiled on the M5 host: record layout, tags, stride and K=534 are measured on the produced artifact only; no M4 hardware execution was possible.
notes:
UNIT copy-records, ground truth re-established on Apple M5 Max (h17), macOS 26.7.1, worktree HEAD abd4370. Nothing under the repo worktree was modified (git status clean); all probes, helpers and temp files live in the unit WD (.../scratchpad/re/copy/). Hardware runs were serial; every boundary point was run at least twice (execution cap points up to six times) and no result flipped; all 33 proposed assertions pass on two consecutive runs and also pass as one spec through the repo's real scripts/evidence-check.sh. Proposed spec lines use @T@ (replace with e.g. /tmp/cp_, not /tmp/pl_). The assertions depend on two NEW repo scripts returned in 'scripts': scripts/decode_copy_records.py and scripts/gen_states_nd.py (state_exec_predict.py is optional).

KEY RE-INTERPRETATIONS (all measured): (1) 0x9365 vs 0x9361 are NOT 'write-side/read-side'. 0x936x without the dim0 field is the UPDATE-ROW copy ([1,dim1] row into the state, one per state, N for plain-input programs, N-1 in the add-chain gen_states_shape.py programs because the producing add writes state 0 directly); the dim0-carrying 0x9365 is the STATE-OUT copy (full [dim0,dim1] updated tensor to its output port) and exists only for state-update tensors that are also program outputs (zero of them when upd_i are not returned). (2) The tag is an elided-default presence mask: tag = 0x9261 + 0x100*[dim1!=1] + 4*[dim0!=1] - [dim1==16]; dim1==1 gives 0x926x (not 'no records'); the only exception found is dim3==256 (no copy records). (3) +0x02/+0x06 in every header are dim3/dim2, not constants. (4) Stride = 8*min(ceil(log2 dim1),4) (dim2=dim3=1), dim0-independent, same on h16g. (5) 'Region' is a u16 rowbits = 16*dim1 mod 2^16 (row width in fp16 bits) shifted into a u32 high half; it is dim1 MiB only where a record's +0x48 happens to hold it (SHORT layout); LONG layout holds 1 MiB at +0x48 and dim1 MiB at +0x44; it wraps to 0 at dim1=4096. (6) SHORT/LONG: for plain-input programs (gen_states.py, gen_states_width.py) exactly the last state-out record is SHORT; for add-chain programs (gen_states_shape.py) the number of trailing SHORTs is 2/1/0 depending on N and ports - no closed form.
